text.p: Venezuela's inflation rate in August was 4.1 percent, up from 3.1 percent in August 1995 but down from 5.0 percent in July, the Central Bank said.
August's inflation rate brings inflation over the past 12 months to 114.7 percent, compared to 52.7 percent in the year to August 1995, the bank said.

It was the third successive drop in the monthly rate since a peak of 12.6 percent in May. The government launched an economic reform program in April which set free currency and interest rates and increased gasoline prices fivefold.
Accumulated inflation for the first eight months of the year now stands at 77.4 percent, compared to 29.4 percent in 1995.

Government officials have predicted that inflation rates will drop steadily to reach no more than two percent per month at the end of the year. Inflation for 1996 will end at 95 percent, compared to 56.6 percent in 1995, they have said.

The central bank said the fall in the monthly inflation rate in August reflected the success of the government's economic program. A reduction in domestic demand caused by the tough program had outweighed the inflationary effect caused by an increase in wholesale taxes from 12.5 to 16.5 percent at the start of the month, the bank added.

"Various expenditures" was the category which registered the highest price rise in August, rising 5.6 percent. "Clothing and shoes" followed with a 4,5 percent rise, "household expenditures" with 4.1 percent and "food, drinks and tobacco" 2.7 percent.
